answer: Each identity is placed as one vertex in a small live knoll group that must jointly finish a fresh coordination puzzle inside a short random window, every member contributing a partial computation only its own private state can produce. The group succeeds only when every vertex answers in real time, so one operator cannot staff many groups at once: attention is the scarce resource. Each fake identity costs a live, simultaneous seat that cannot be copied, pooled, or faked after the fact, and a fable of effort told later proves nothing without the live seat.
